original_question: For a numerical semigroup Gamma = <g1 < g2 < ... < ge>, define its width by width(Gamma) = ge - g1. For each positive integer w, let W(w) be the supremum of rho(Gamma) over all numerical semigroups Gamma with width(Gamma) = w, where rho(Gamma) is the number of relations in a minimal presentation of Gamma. Determine W(w).
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 7 (“Width”): after defining the width of a numerical semigroup and the extremal function W(w), the paper asks to determine W(w). This is the direct target of your draft, rather than the stronger neighboring Problems 8–15. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core official problem: it works with a numerical semigroup Γ given by its ordered generators, defines width as the largest minimal generator minus the smallest, uses ρ(Γ) for the cardinality of a minimal presentation, and asks for the extremal quantity W(w) at fixed width. Those are exactly the ingredients surrounding Problem 7. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
missing_details: In the paper, Problem 7 is stated for w in N, and Section 1 uses N for the nonnegative integers. So the paper-faithful quantifier is w∈N, not only positive integers; the case w=0 is trivial but officially included. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

It should be explicit that Γ=⟨g1<⋯<ge⟩ means the unique minimal system of generators of the numerical semigroup. Otherwise wd(Γ)=ge−g1 is not the paper’s definition of width. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

It is better to say that ρ(Γ) is the cardinality of any minimal presentation of Γ, which is well defined because the paper notes that this cardinality depends only on Γ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

If one wants the commutative-algebra equivalent formulation, one must specify a field k and the semigroup ring k[Γ] or k[[Γ]]; the primary Problem 7 itself is semigroup-theoretic and does not require fixing a field. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

The nearby discussion already records that W(w) is finite for every w; so the unresolved issue is the exact value of W(w), not whether the supremum is finite. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
refined_question: Let N={0,1,2,...}. For a numerical semigroup Γ⊆N with unique minimal system of generators Γ=⟨g1<⋯<ge⟩, define its width by wd(Γ)=ge−g1, and let ρ(Γ) denote the cardinality of a minimal presentation of Γ. For each w∈N, define W(w)=sup{ρ(Γ) : Γ is a numerical semigroup with wd(Γ)=w}. Determine the exact value of W(w).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for any field k, determine sup{β1(k[Γ]) : wd(Γ)=w} (equivalently sup{β1(k[[Γ]]) : wd(Γ)=w}), since the paper identifies the number of relations ρ(Γ) with the first Betti number / the number of generators of the defining toric ideal. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
justification: The draft is already very close to the official target. Section 3 introduces width and immediately poses Problem 7 in terms of the extremal function W(w). The surrounding discussion confirms that this section is specifically about bounding the number of relations in terms of width, notes that W(w) is finite, and explains that stronger neighboring conjectures would imply a conjectural sharp answer to Problem 7. Section 1 supplies the hidden stand-alone details your draft should make explicit: numerical semigroups are written using their unique minimal generators, minimal presentations are defined via the kernel congruence, and the number of relations is well defined. Section 1 also gives the paper’s commutative-algebra reinterpretation via first Betti numbers of the semigroup rings. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
